rich/console.py:1154-1168 follows the show_cursor pattern (rich/console.py:1143-1152): guard on self.is_terminal, delegate to self.control(Control.title(...)), return bool. Rendering logic stays in control.py and the Windows renderer, as in the reference.

The feature uses the existing extension points: CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT (rich/control.py:33), the ControlType enum (rich/segment.py:52), the Control classmethod factory pattern (rich/control.py:151-161, mirroring alt_screen at 143-149), and the legacy_windows_render if/elif dispatch (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56).

Without this entry rendering would raise KeyError, so the registration is present.

The legacy Windows path forwards the title to term.set_title (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56), so the Windows-console feature is covered as in the reference.

The patch's docstring (rich/console.py:1156-1158) omits the reference's caveats about persistence and terminal support, but its statement that Rich cannot restore titles covers the main limitation. Documentation depth is not a behavioural requirement.
